rule_changes.Current text: A descriptive definite that names a kind of thing but not which one ("the Bitcoin ETF", "the major-bank stablecoin consortium", "the open-access version", "the infrastructure", "the new model") makes the claim Context-dependent: the reader must already know which ETF, consortium, version or product is meant. Applies to countable things, not to abstract or mass nouns ("the regulatory clearance", "the market").
rule_changes.Proposed text: A descriptive definite that names a kind of thing but not which one ("the Bitcoin ETF", "the major-bank stablecoin consortium", "the open-access version", "the infrastructure", "the new model") makes the claim Context-dependent: the reader must already know which ETF, consortium, version or product is meant. It applies to countable things, not to abstract or mass nouns ("the regulatory clearance", "the market"). It does not apply to a group that every reader knows by its standing role ("the press pool", "the press corps"). A capitalised phrase that names no body readers know is still a kind of thing and not which one, so it does make the claim Context-dependent.
